column4: Test Steps

column3: Validate operating system and CPU/GPU platform
column4: Reference: docs/user-guide/get-started/system-requirements.md
column5: Host runs Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later and has the intended Intel Core Ultra platform with integrated Intel graphics. GPU driver has been successfully installed.

column3: Validate RAM swap and free disk capacity
column4: Check memory: 1. free -h  2. swapon -show  3. df -h ~
column5: At least 64 GB RAM + 32 GB enabled swap and 128 GB available disk are present for the default Qwen3.6-35B-A3B FP8 60k deployment.

column3: Start and health-check the on-device model serving
column4: 1.Follow the get-started.md guide: Step 1 — Start the dependent external services to deploy services, wait for the first-start model download and compilation to finish. Models should be downloaded to ~/model/huggingface/hub
column5: The vllm-ipex-serving container is running well, and the curl response is OK.

column4: 2. Check container status: docker ps
3. Run: curl -fsS http://localhost:41091/v1/models

4. Curl with multimodal requests: curl http://localhost:41091/v1/chat/completions -XPOST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{     "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B",     "messages": [       {         "role": "user",         "content": [           {             "type": "text",             "text": "Describe the image."           },           {             "type": "image_url",             "image_url": {               "url": "http://farm6.staticflickr.com/5268/5602445367_3504763978_z.jpg"             }           }         ]       }     ],     "max_tokens": 512   }'
1. Run: curl -fsS http://localhost:8192/v1/health
column5: Both health endpoints return successful JSON responses, the multilevel-video-understanding and videostream-analytics services remain running.

column4: 2. Run: curl -fsS http://localhost:8999/health

column3: Start and health-check the MCP server
column4: 1. Follow get-started.md Step 2: copy config.yaml.example to config.yaml, customize it if needed, and run: bash scripts/mcp-server/start.sh config.yaml
column5: The launcher completes successfully; the MCP initialize request returns an mcp-session-id; the events health endpoint returns status healthy; smartbuilding.db and the MCP log exist.

column4: 2. Initialize MCP and save response headers: curl -fsS -D /tmp/asc-mcp-headers -o /tmp/asc-mcp-init.json -X POST http://localhost:3100/mcp -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"testplan","version":"1.0"}}}'
3. Run: grep -i '^mcp-session-id:' /tmp/asc-mcp-headers
4. Run: curl -fsS http://localhost:3101/health
5. Check database existing: ~/.mcp-smartbuilding/smartbuilding.db
1. Run: curl -fsS http://localhost:8192/v1/tasks | jq -e '[.tasks[].name]'
column5: The command exits successfully and confirms that fridge_monitor, child_safety_monitor, and elder_wakeup_monitor are registered.

column4: 2. Confirm config.yaml contains use_case_dict entries named fridge, child_safety, and elder_wakeup.

column3: Connect an agent host and discover Smart Building tools
column4: 1. Follow get-started.md Step 3 to configure a compatible MCP client with transport streamable-http and URL http://localhost:3100/mcp.
column5: The client connects without an MCP transport error and exposes the complete smartbuilding_* tool set. It can list monitors and bundled use cases; an empty monitor list is valid before a camera is registered.

column4: 2. Follow full guides in the section to setup OpenClaw
3. From :18789 controUI, ask the agent some related questions about Smart Building
Question: “List the available Smart Building tools”
Question: “List current Smart Building use cases”
1. Prepare a valid RTSP video stream as a camera monitor source, run: bash scripts/helpers/local_video_to_rtsp.sh {your-local-video-path}, you can have a RTSP stream: rtsp://localhost:8555/live
column5: The RTSP stream remains available; the agent successfully registers the monitor as cam_child_safety with source_url rtsp://localhost:8555/live and use_case child_safety; the monitor appears in the monitor list with online status and no MCP tool error.

column4: 2. From :18789 controUI, ask the agent to register a camera monitor with the bundled use cases
Question: “Register a camera source: rtsp://localhost:8555/live, use case id: child_safety”
Precondition: an online monitor is runing for a while to get some events inserted into database ( ~/.mcp-smartbuilding/smartbuilding.db)
column5: The agent successfully invokes smartbuilding_generate_report for the cam_child_safety monitor; the response is a daily report for the current date and summarizes the monitor's stored events without an MCP tool error.

column4: From :18789 controUI, ask the agent to generate report
Question: “Generate today's report"

column3: Receive monitor alert updates through MCP subscription
column4: Precondition: register a user-provided monitor that can produce an alert with one of the bundled use cases. (e.g., child_safety, elder_wakeup)
column5: The subscription succeeds; the SSE stream receives notifications/resources/updated for the subscribed monitor; resources/read with the previous latestId returns the new delivered alert and advances latestId.

column4: 1. Follow docs/user-guide/get-started/mcp-subscription-reference.md(Terminal Example) to initialize a session and subscribe notifications.
2. In another terminal, copy the session ID printed above, set it as SID, then open the SSE stream and keep it open to receive notifications from MCP server.

column3: Register a custom use case by conversation
column4: 1. Follow docs/user-guide/get-started/register-new-use-case.md and ask the connected agent to create a uniquely named test use case; complete Q1/Q2 and approve the final schema.
column5: The agent completes register_task and register without restarting the core services; the use case appears in the server use-case list and config.yaml; its video-summary task is available from /v1/tasks. If an RTSP URL was supplied, the monitor is also registered.

column4: 2. Verify the agent reports successful task registration and use-case registration.
3. Verify config.yaml contains the new use_case_dict entry.
4. Run: curl -fsS http://localhost:8192/v1/tasks and verify the new video-summary task name is present.
